name: Folate/direct/folate route
description: Folate-dependent GAR formylation, direct AIR carboxylation, and folate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Folate/direct/formate route
description: Folate-dependent GAR formylation, direct AIR carboxylation, and formate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Folate/two-step/folate route
description: Folate-dependent GAR formylation, two-step AIR carboxylation, and folate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Folate/two-step/formate route
description: Folate-dependent GAR formylation, two-step AIR carboxylation, and formate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Formate/direct/folate route
description: Formate-dependent GAR formylation, direct AIR carboxylation, and folate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Formate/direct/formate route
description: Formate-dependent GAR formylation, direct AIR carboxylation, and formate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Formate/two-step/folate route
description: Formate-dependent GAR formylation, two-step AIR carboxylation, and folate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Formate/two-step/formate route
description: Formate-dependent GAR formylation, two-step AIR carboxylation, and formate-dependent AICAR formylation.

name: Adenylosuccinate route
description: IMP to AMP through adenylosuccinate synthase and adenylosuccinate lyase.

name: XMP route
description: IMP to GMP through IMP dehydrogenase and glutamine-dependent GMP synthase.

name: Fumarate-dependent DHODH route
description: De novo UMP biosynthesis using fumarate-dependent dihydroorotate oxidation.

name: NAD-dependent DHODH route
description: De novo UMP biosynthesis using NAD-dependent dihydroorotate oxidation.

name: Quinone-dependent DHODH route
description: De novo UMP biosynthesis using quinone-dependent dihydroorotate oxidation.

name: Glutamine-dependent CTP synthase route
description: UTP to CTP through the complete glutamine-dependent CTP synthase reaction.

name: Phosphorylated serine route
description: 3-phosphoglycerate oxidation, transamination and dephosphorylation to L-serine.

name: Serine hydroxymethyltransferase route
description: Folate-dependent removal of the serine hydroxymethyl group to give glycine.

name: Aspartate kinase route
description: Aspartate phosphorylation followed by NADPH-dependent reduction to the 4-semialdehyde.

name: NAD-dependent homoserine dehydrogenase route
description: Reduction of L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde to L-homoserine using NADH.

name: NADP-dependent homoserine dehydrogenase route
description: Reduction of L-aspartate 4-semialdehyde to L-homoserine using NADPH.

name: Homoserine kinase route
description: Homoserine phosphorylation followed by threonine synthase.

name: Succinyl/transsulfuration/cobalamin route
description: O-succinylhomoserine transsulfuration with cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase.

name: Succinyl/transsulfuration/cobalamin-independent route
description: O-succinylhomoserine transsulfuration with cobalamin-independent methionine synthase.

name: Acetyl/transsulfuration/cobalamin route
description: O-acetylhomoserine transsulfuration with cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase.

name: Acetyl/transsulfuration/cobalamin-independent route
description: O-acetylhomoserine transsulfuration with cobalamin-independent methionine synthase.

name: Phospho/transsulfuration/cobalamin route
description: Plant O-phosphohomoserine transsulfuration with cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase.

name: Phospho/transsulfuration/cobalamin-independent route
description: Plant O-phosphohomoserine transsulfuration with cobalamin-independent methionine synthase.

name: Succinyl/sulfhydrylation/cobalamin route
description: Direct sulfide incorporation into O-succinylhomoserine with cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase.

name: Succinyl/sulfhydrylation/cobalamin-independent route
description: Direct sulfide incorporation into O-succinylhomoserine with cobalamin-independent methionine synthase.

name: Acetyl/sulfhydrylation/cobalamin route
description: Direct sulfide incorporation into O-acetylhomoserine with cobalamin-dependent methionine synthase.

name: Acetyl/sulfhydrylation/cobalamin-independent route
description: Direct sulfide incorporation into O-acetylhomoserine with cobalamin-independent methionine synthase.

name: O-acetylserine sulfhydrylation route
description: Serine acetylation followed by sulfide incorporation.

name: Serine-dependent reverse transsulfuration route
description: Cystathionine beta-synthase acting on L-serine, then cystathionine gamma-lyase.

name: O-acetylserine-dependent reverse transsulfuration route
description: Serine acetylation, cystathionine beta-synthase acting on O-acetyl-L-serine, then cystathionine gamma-lyase.

name: Xylose isomerase route
description: Isomerisation to D-xylulose and phosphorylation to D-xylulose 5-phosphate.

name: L-arabinose isomerase route
description: Isomerisation to L-ribulose, phosphorylation, and epimerisation to D-xylulose 5-phosphate.

name: L-fucose isomerase route
description: Isomerisation to L-fuculose, phosphorylation, and aldol cleavage.

name: L-rhamnose isomerase route
description: Isomerisation to L-rhamnulose, phosphorylation, and aldol cleavage.

name: Leloir route
description: Mutarotation, galactokinase, uridylyltransferase, and UDP-glucose regeneration.

name: N-acetylglucosamine kinase route
description: Phosphorylation, deacetylation, and deamination to fructose 6-phosphate.

name: N-acetylneuraminate lyase route
description: Lyase cleavage to N-acetylmannosamine, phosphorylation, epimerisation, deacetylation, and deamination.

name: Galacturonate isomerase route
description: Isomerisation to keto-D-tagaturonate, reduction to D-altronate and dehydration to the Entner-Doudoroff branchpoint.

name: Glucuronate isomerase route
description: Isomerisation to keto-D-fructuronate, reduction to D-mannonate and dehydration to the Entner-Doudoroff branchpoint.

name: ABC importer route
description: ATP-driven translocation by a periplasmic-binding-protein-dependent importer.

name: ABC importer route
description: ATP-driven translocation by a periplasmic-binding-protein-dependent importer.

name: Endo-xylanase and beta-xylosidase route
description: Backbone endohydrolysis then exo-acting release of D-xylose, with acetyl de-blocking as accessory chemistry.

name: Arabinofuranosidase route
description: Hydrolysis of alpha-L-arabinofuranosyl side chains.

name: Alpha-amylase and alpha-glucosidase route
description: Backbone endohydrolysis then exo-acting release of D-glucose, with alpha-1,6 debranching as accessory chemistry.

name: M9 microbial collagenase route
description: Direct cleavage of the collagen triple helix by a secreted family M9 collagenase.

name: Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex route
description: NAD-dependent oxidative decarboxylation by the multienzyme dehydrogenase complex.

name: Pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase route
description: Ferredoxin-dependent oxidative decarboxylation; the oxygen-sensitive route of anaerobes.

name: Pyruvate formate-lyase route
description: Radical-mediated non-oxidative cleavage releasing formate, requiring the activating enzyme to install the glycyl radical.

name: Phosphotransacetylase and acetate kinase route
description: Transfer of the acetyl group to phosphate and substrate-level phosphorylation of ADP, yielding acetate and ATP.

name: Acetyl-CoA condensation with CoA-transferase release
description: Thiolytic condensation of two acetyl-CoA, reduction through 3-hydroxybutanoyl-CoA and crotonoyl-CoA to butanoyl-CoA, and CoA transfer onto acetate to release butanoate.

name: Lactaldehyde reductase route
description: NADH-dependent reduction of (S)-lactaldehyde to (S)-propane-1,2-diol.

name: Propanediol utilisation route
description: Coenzyme-B12-dependent dehydration to propanal, CoA-acylating oxidation to propanoyl-CoA, and substrate-level phosphorylation to propanoate.

name: Acrylate route
description: CoA transfer from propanoyl-CoA onto lactate, dehydration to acryloyl-CoA, and reduction back to propanoyl-CoA, with propanoate released by the transfer step.

name: NAD-dependent lactate dehydrogenase route
description: Reduction of pyruvate by NADH to (S)-lactate, regenerating NAD+ for glycolysis.

name: Lactate racemase route
description: Interconversion of the two lactate enantiomers by the nickel-pincer racemase LarA. One traversal, not a mirrored pair: a flipped copy would complete on the same marker.

name: Malolactic enzyme route
description: Direct decarboxylation of (S)-malate to (S)-lactate, without a free pyruvate intermediate and without a separate decarboxylase.

name: Citrate lyase and oxaloacetate decarboxylase route
description: Cleavage of citrate to oxaloacetate and acetate by the holo-citrate lyase complex, followed by decarboxylation of oxaloacetate to pyruvate.

name: Bifunctional acetaldehyde/alcohol dehydrogenase route
description: Reduction of acetyl-CoA to acetaldehyde and of acetaldehyde to ethanol, both steps carried by AdhE.

name: Acetolactate synthase and decarboxylase route
description: Condensation of two pyruvate to (2S)-2-acetolactate and its decarboxylation to (R)-acetoin. The synthase step is curated but not required.

name: GTP and ribulose 5-phosphate route
description: The canonical bacterial route. The 3.1.3.104 phosphatase step is curated as not required: the chemistry is universal but no orthology group covers it across bacteria, and requiring it would call 5261 genomes that carry every other step riboflavin-negative.

name: 4-amino-4-deoxychorismate route
description: Amination of chorismate and elimination of pyruvate. PabA, the glutamine amidotransferase subunit, is interchangeable with TrpG and is not required as evidence.

name: Pterin and 4-aminobenzoate route
description: GTP cyclohydrolase I through dihydrofolate reductase.

name: ThiC route
description: Phosphomethylpyrimidine synthase followed by ThiD-mediated phosphorylation.

name: Tyrosine-dependent ThiH route
description: ThiH cleaves L-tyrosine to 2-iminoacetate, which thiazole synthase condenses with DXP.

name: Glycine-dependent ThiO route
description: ThiO oxidises glycine to 2-iminoacetate, which thiazole synthase condenses with DXP.

name: Thiamine phosphate synthase route
description: Condensation of the pyrimidine diphosphate and the thiazole phosphate.

name: ThiD and ThiM route
description: Two successive ThiD phosphorylations of the pyrimidine and one ThiM phosphorylation of the thiazole.

name: PanB, PanE, PanD and PanC route
description: Ketopantoate formation and reduction, beta-alanine formation, and ligation. The reduction accepts IlvC as well as PanE, which is a non-homologous replacement for that reaction rather than a widened marker.

name: PdxS and PdxT route
description: One reaction catalysed by a two-subunit complex.

name: Epd, PdxB, SerC, PdxA and PdxJ route
description: The transamination is curated in reverse relative to the Rhea master, which is written in the direction that consumes 4-phosphohydroxy-L-threonine.

name: S-adenosylmethionine-dependent transaminase route
description: The BioA route used by Proteobacteria, in which the amino donor is S-adenosylmethionine.

name: Lysine-dependent transaminase route
description: The BioA route used by Bacillus and many Firmicutes, in which the amino donor is L-lysine.

name: L-aspartate oxidase route
description: NadB oxidises L-aspartate to iminosuccinate using molecular oxygen; the same enzyme uses fumarate anaerobically, which gifter does not curate.

name: Aspartate dehydrogenase route
description: NadX forms iminosuccinate with NAD as the acceptor, the route used by many anaerobes and archaea.

name: Quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase route
description: A single reaction.

name: Ammonia-dependent NAD synthetase route
description: NadE amidates deamido-NAD using ammonium.

name: Glutamine-dependent NAD synthetase route
description: The glutamine-hydrolysing synthetase, which is the only form in many organisms.

name: Nicotinate phosphoribosyltransferase route
description: A single ATP-dependent reaction.

name: Anaerobic early-cobalt-insertion route
description: Cobalt is inserted into sirohydrochlorin before ring contraction. The chelatase and the two reductase steps are curated in reverse relative to their Rhea masters, which are written in the cobalt-releasing and oxidising directions.

name: Aerobic late-cobalt-insertion route
description: The ring is completed as the cobalt-free hydrogenobyrinate, amidated, and only then loaded with cobalt by the three-subunit CobNST chelatase. CobG makes the route strictly oxygen-dependent.

name: Adenosylation and aminopropanol arm route
description: Cobalt adenosylation, cobyric acid synthesis, and condensation with (R)-1-aminopropan-2-yl phosphate.

name: Dimethylbenzimidazole loop route
description: Guanylyltransferase, phosphoribosyltransferase, ribazole phosphatase and ribazoletransferase.

name: BluB route
description: One oxygen-dependent reaction that dismantles reduced FMN.

name: Classical men route
description: Isochorismate through the naphthoate, then prenylation and methylation. The isochorismate synthase reaction accepts EntC as well as MenF: the two enzymes catalyse the same reaction, and route completeness supplies the pathway specificity.

name: Futalosine route
description: The chorismate-dehydratase route of Helicobacter, Campylobacter and Streptomyces, which shares only the terminal prenylation and methylation with the classical route. The deaminase step is not required, because the modified futalosine route omits it.

name: Citrate synthase and aconitase route
description: Condensation to citrate and isomerisation to the isocitrate branchpoint.

name: 2-oxoglutarate dehydrogenase complex route
description: Irreversible oxidative decarboxylation to succinyl-CoA by the multienzyme complex, then substrate-level phosphorylation to succinate.

name: Ferredoxin oxidoreductase route
description: Ferredoxin-dependent oxidative decarboxylation to succinyl-CoA, then substrate-level phosphorylation. The same enzyme runs reductively in the reductive citric acid cycle.

name: 2-oxoglutarate decarboxylase bypass, NAD-dependent
description: Decarboxylation to succinate semialdehyde followed by NAD-dependent oxidation to succinate. No succinyl-CoA intermediate and no substrate-level phosphorylation.

name: 2-oxoglutarate decarboxylase bypass, NADP-dependent
description: As the NAD bypass, with the NADP-dependent succinate-semialdehyde dehydrogenase.

name: Quinone-dependent succinate/fumarate couple
description: One traversal of the couple, written from succinate to fumarate. The GIFT declares no direction; the route records the orientation relative to how Rhea writes the equation.

name: Fumarase and NAD-malate dehydrogenase route
description: Hydration of fumarate to (S)-malate followed by NAD-dependent oxidation to oxaloacetate. Both steps are reversible.

name: Fumarase and malate:quinone oxidoreductase route
description: Hydration of fumarate to (S)-malate followed by quinone-dependent oxidation to oxaloacetate. The second step is effectively unidirectional.

name: Shikimate pathway
description: The seven-step sequence from phosphoenolpyruvate and erythrose 4-phosphate. The shikimate dehydrogenase step is curated as not required: K00014 is annotated in 5585 bacteria while every other step of the route is annotated in 8461 to 9149, and requiring it drops the route from 7644 to 5420 bacteria, removing 201 of 213 cyanobacteria and 1061 of 1642 Actinomycetota. Those organisms make aromatic amino acids and carry a shikimate dehydrogenase gene; KEGG simply does not assign it to a KO.

name: Isochorismate route
description: Isomerisation of chorismate to isochorismate followed by pyruvate elimination. The only known route from chorismate to salicylate, and the same two transformations whether a genome uses separate PchA and PchB proteins or a single bifunctional salicylate synthase.

name: Indole-3-acetamide route
description: Oxidative decarboxylation of tryptophan to indole-3-acetamide by IaaM, then hydrolysis to indole-3-acetate. Aerobic, because tryptophan 2-monooxygenase consumes molecular oxygen.

name: Urate oxidase route
description: Cofactor-independent urate oxidase, then hydrolysis of 5-hydroxyisourate and decarboxylation to (S)-allantoin.

name: HpxO urate hydroxylase route
description: Flavin-dependent urate hydroxylase in place of urate oxidase, converging on the same hydrolysis and decarboxylation.

name: Allantoicase route
description: Allantoinase then allantoicase, releasing one urea before the ureidoglycolate lyase releases the second.

name: Allantoate deiminase route
description: Allantoinase, then deamination of allantoate and hydrolysis of ureidoglycine, releasing two ammonium that the allantoicase route does not.

name: Urease route
description: Nickel-dependent hydrolysis of urea to ammonium and hydrogencarbonate.

name: NasAC with NAD(P)H nitrite reductase
description: Assimilatory nitrate reductase then a NAD(P)H-dependent nitrite reductase.

name: NasAC with ferredoxin nitrite reductase
description: Assimilatory nitrate reductase then ferredoxin-nitrite reductase.

name: NarB with NAD(P)H nitrite reductase
description: Ferredoxin-nitrate reductase then a NAD(P)H-dependent nitrite reductase.

name: NarB with ferredoxin nitrite reductase
description: The fully ferredoxin-linked route, characteristic of cyanobacteria.

name: Monooxygenase with ferredoxin dehydrogenase
description: Glycine betaine monooxygenase then the ferredoxin-dependent dimethylglycine dehydrogenase.

name: Monooxygenase with ETF dehydrogenase
description: Glycine betaine monooxygenase then the electron-transfer-flavoprotein dimethylglycine dehydrogenase.

name: Monooxygenase with dimethylglycine oxidase
description: Glycine betaine monooxygenase then the oxygen-dependent dimethylglycine oxidase.

name: Sarcosine oxidase route
description: Oxygen-dependent oxidative demethylation, by either the heterotetrameric or the monomeric enzyme.

name: Ferredoxin dehydrogenase route
description: Ferredoxin-dependent demethylation by the same DgcAB pair that acts on dimethylglycine.

name: Creatininase route
description: Cyclic amide hydrolysis to creatine, then amidinohydrolysis to sarcosine and urea.

name: Carnitine monooxygenase route
description: Rieske oxygenase cleavage of carnitine, releasing free trimethylamine.

name: Carnitine dehydrogenase route
description: Oxidation to 3-dehydrocarnitine, retro-Claisen cleavage to betainyl-CoA, and thioester hydrolysis to glycine betaine.

name: Methylamine dehydrogenase route
description: Oxidative deamination by the tryptophan-tryptophylquinone enzyme.

name: Taurine dioxygenase route
description: 2-oxoglutarate-dependent desulfonation, releasing sulfite and leaving the nitrogen on aminoacetaldehyde.

name: Transaminase route
description: Taurine-pyruvate transamination to sulfoacetaldehyde, then acetyltransferase cleavage. The nitrogen leaves as L-alanine.

name: Dehydrogenase route
description: Taurine dehydrogenase deamination to sulfoacetaldehyde, then acetyltransferase cleavage. The nitrogen leaves as ammonium.

name: ABC importer route
description: ATP-driven translocation by a periplasmic-binding-protein-dependent importer.

name: GS-GOGAT route, NADPH
description: Glutamine synthetase fixes ammonium onto glutamate, and NADPH-dependent glutamate synthase transfers the amide onto 2-oxoglutarate.

name: GS-GOGAT route, ferredoxin
description: As the NADPH route, with the ferredoxin-dependent glutamate synthase.

name: NADP-glutamate dehydrogenase route
description: Direct reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate. Lower affinity for ammonium than GS-GOGAT and independent of it.

name: NAD-glutamate dehydrogenase route
description: Direct reductive amination of 2-oxoglutarate by the NAD-dependent enzyme.

name: Benzoate 1,2-dioxygenase route
description: Ring dihydroxylation by the benABC oxygenase and decarboxylating dehydrogenation by benD.

name: Anthranilate 1,2-dioxygenase route
description: Single-step oxidative deamination and decarboxylation to catechol.

name: Multicomponent phenol 2-monooxygenase route
description: Single-step hydroxylation by the six-subunit phenol hydroxylase.

name: Intradiol cleavage route
description: Catechol 1,2-dioxygenase, muconate cycloisomerase, muconolactone isomerase and enol-lactone hydrolysis.

name: Succinyl-CoA transferase route
description: CoA transfer from succinyl-CoA onto 3-oxoadipate by the pcaIJ transferase.

name: Beta-ketothiolase route
description: Thiolysis of 3-oxoadipyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA and acetyl-CoA.

name: Extradiol cleavage, hydrolytic branch
description: Catechol 2,3-dioxygenase followed by hydrolysis of the semialdehyde, releasing formate.

name: Extradiol cleavage, 4-oxalocrotonate branch
description: Catechol 2,3-dioxygenase followed by oxidation of the semialdehyde, tautomerisation and decarboxylation.

name: Hydratase-aldolase-dehydrogenase route
description: Hydration to 4-hydroxy-2-oxopentanoate, retro-aldol cleavage to pyruvate and acetaldehyde, and acylating oxidation to acetyl-CoA.

name: Aerobic phenylacetyl-CoA epoxidase route
description: CoA ligation, ring epoxidation, oxepin isomerisation, hydrolytic ring opening and beta-oxidation to 3-oxoadipyl-CoA.

name: Ring-hydroxylating dioxygenase route
description: Dihydroxylation by the hcaEF oxygenase and dehydrogenation of the cis-diol by hcaB.

name: Flavin monooxygenase route
description: Single-step hydroxylation by mhpA.

name: Extradiol cleavage and hydrolysis route
description: Ring cleavage by mhpB and hydrolysis by mhpC, releasing succinate.

name: Glutamine synthetase route
description: Single ATP-dependent amidation. The same reaction is the first step of the GS-GOGAT route of ammonium assimilation, where the glutamine formed is consumed internally by glutamate synthase rather than released.

name: Alanine transaminase route
description: Transamination of pyruvate using L-glutamate, or L-valine in the case of transaminase C.

name: Alanine dehydrogenase route
description: Reductive amination of pyruvate with ammonium. The enzyme is freely reversible and runs catabolically in several Firmicutes; gifter claims the encoded chemistry between the boundaries, not the direction of flux.

name: Aspartate aminotransferase route
description: Reversible transamination from L-glutamate, run in the aspartate-forming direction.

name: Ammonia-dependent ligase route
description: AsnA amidates aspartate using free ammonium.

name: Glutamine-hydrolysing synthase route
description: AsnB amidates aspartate using the amide nitrogen of L-glutamine.

name: Succinylated route
description: Succinyl protection of the tetrahydrodipicolinate amino group, transamination, desuccinylation and epimerisation. The dominant route in Proteobacteria.

name: Acetylated route
description: The same chemistry with acetyl rather than succinyl protection; found mainly in Bacillus.

name: Diaminopimelate dehydrogenase route
description: Direct reductive amination to meso-diaminopimelate, replacing four steps and needing no epimerase.

name: LL-diaminopimelate aminotransferase route
description: Single-step transamination to LL-diaminopimelate followed by epimerisation.

name: Diaminopimelate decarboxylase route
description: Single PLP-dependent decarboxylation.

name: Acetohydroxyacid route
description: Condensation of two pyruvates, reductive isomerisation, and dehydration.

name: Branched-chain aminotransferase route
description: Transamination from L-glutamate, run in the valine-forming direction.

name: Isopropylmalate route
description: Acetyl-CoA condensation, isomerisation through 2-isopropylmaleate, oxidative decarboxylation and transamination.

name: Citramalate route
description: Acetyl-CoA condensation with pyruvate, isomerisation by the isopropylmalate isomerase acting on citramalate, and oxidative decarboxylation.

name: Acetohydroxyacid route
description: Condensation with pyruvate, reductive isomerisation, dehydration and transamination.

name: Prephenate dehydratase route
description: Chorismate mutase, decarboxylative dehydration to phenylpyruvate, and transamination.

name: NAD-dependent prephenate dehydrogenase route
description: Chorismate mutase, NAD-dependent oxidative decarboxylation, and transamination.

name: NADP-dependent prephenate dehydrogenase route
description: The same chemistry with the NADP-dependent dehydrogenase, a separate orthology group.

name: Anthranilate route
description: Anthranilate synthesis, phosphoribosyl transfer, isomerisation, ring closure and the tryptophan synthase reaction.

name: Canonical histidine route
description: Phosphoribosyl transfer to ATP, pyrophosphohydrolysis, ring opening, isomerisation, glutamine-dependent cyclisation, dehydration, transamination, dephosphorylation and the two histidinol oxidations.

name: Glutamate 5-kinase route
description: Glutamate phosphorylation and reduction to the 5-semialdehyde, which cyclises spontaneously, followed by reduction of the pyrroline to proline. The bifunctional P5C synthetase is an alternative system for the first two reactions.

name: Linear acetylornithine deacetylase route
description: Acetylation, phosphorylation, reduction, transamination and hydrolytic deacetylation.

name: Cyclic ornithine acetyltransferase route
description: The same chemistry, but the acetyl group is transferred from acetylornithine back onto glutamate rather than hydrolysed, which conserves it.

name: Citrulline route
description: Ornithine carbamoyltransferase, argininosuccinate synthase and argininosuccinate lyase.

name: Arginine deiminase route
description: Arginine deiminase, ornithine carbamoyltransferase run in the phosphorolytic direction, and carbamate kinase run in the ATP-forming direction.

name: Formimidoylglutamase route
description: Histidase, urocanate hydratase, imidazolonepropionase and formimidoylglutamase.

name: Threonine ammonia-lyase route
description: Single PLP-dependent deamination.

name: L-serine ammonia-lyase route
description: Single deamination by the iron-sulfur or PLP-dependent serine dehydratase.

name: Glutamate decarboxylase route
description: Single PLP-dependent decarboxylation.

name: Tryptophanase route
description: Single PLP-dependent beta-elimination.

name: Methionine gamma-lyase route
description: Single PLP-dependent gamma-elimination.

name: Cysteine desulfidase route
description: Single beta-elimination by a dedicated L-cysteine desulfidase.

name: Glycine reductase route
description: Single reductive deamination by the multi-subunit selenoprotein complex.

name: D-proline reductase route
description: Proline racemisation followed by reductive ring opening.

name: NADP-isocitrate dehydrogenase route
description: NADP-dependent oxidative decarboxylation to 2-oxoglutarate.

name: NAD-isocitrate dehydrogenase route
description: NAD-dependent oxidative decarboxylation to 2-oxoglutarate.

name: Direct isocitrate-lyase and malate-synthase route
description: Cleavage to succinate and glyoxylate followed by condensation of glyoxylate with acetyl-CoA to malate.

name: Molybdenum nitrogenase route
description: NifHDK catalysis with NifEN and NifB cofactor assembly.

name: Vanadium nitrogenase route
description: VnfHDGK catalysis with VnfEN and NifB cofactor assembly.

name: APS branch with NADPH sulfite reductase
description: Sulfate activation to APS, direct APS reduction to sulfite, and NADPH-dependent reduction to sulfide.

name: APS branch with ferredoxin sulfite reductase
description: Sulfate activation to APS, direct APS reduction to sulfite, and ferredoxin-dependent reduction to sulfide.

name: PAPS branch with NADPH sulfite reductase
description: Sulfate activation and APS phosphorylation, PAPS reduction to sulfite, and NADPH-dependent reduction to sulfide.

name: PAPS branch with ferredoxin sulfite reductase
description: Sulfate activation and APS phosphorylation, PAPS reduction to sulfite, and ferredoxin-dependent reduction to sulfide.

name: EctABC route
description: EctB forms L-2,4-diaminobutanoate from ASA, EctA acetylates it, and EctC cyclises the acetylated intermediate to L-ectoine.

name: Classical HemF-HemY route
description: Oxygen-dependent coproporphyrinogen and protoporphyrinogen oxidation followed by ferrochelation.

name: Classical HemF-HemG route
description: Oxygen-dependent HemF followed by menaquinone-dependent HemG and ferrochelation.

name: Classical HemF-HemJ route
description: Oxygen-dependent HemF followed by HemJ with an unresolved electron acceptor and ferrochelation.

name: Classical HemN-HemY route
description: Oxygen-independent HemN followed by oxygen-dependent HemY and ferrochelation.

name: Classical HemN-HemG route
description: Oxygen-independent radical-SAM HemN and menaquinone-dependent HemG followed by ferrochelation.

name: Classical HemN-HemJ route
description: Oxygen-independent HemN and HemJ followed by ferrochelation; the HemJ electron acceptor remains abstract.

name: Coproporphyrin-dependent HemY-HemH-HemQ route
description: HemY oxidises coproporphyrinogen, HemH inserts iron into coproporphyrin, and HemQ converts coproheme to heme b.

name: EntC-EntB-EntA catecholate head route
description: Chorismate isomerisation, isochorismate hydrolysis and dehydrogenation form 2,3-dihydroxybenzoate.

name: EntB-EntD-EntE-EntF assembly route
description: The activated aryl carrier, phosphopantetheinyl transferase, DHB ligase and serine-activating NRPS jointly assemble enterobactin.

name: BetA-BetB route
description: Acceptor-dependent choline dehydrogenase followed by NAD-dependent betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase.

name: GbsB-GbsA route
description: NAD-dependent choline dehydrogenase followed by NAD-dependent betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase.

name: Choline monooxygenase-BADH route
description: Ferredoxin- and oxygen-dependent choline monooxygenase followed by NAD-dependent betaine-aldehyde dehydrogenase.

name: Choline oxidase route
description: One choline oxidase catalyses both oxygen-dependent oxidations from choline through betaine aldehyde to glycine betaine.

name: Siroheme route from uroporphyrinogen III
description: Two SAM-dependent methyl transfers, precorrin-2 dehydrogenation and iron insertion form siroheme through multifunctional or split enzyme systems.

name: Endochitinase and hexosaminidase route
description: Backbone endohydrolysis then exo-acting release of GlcNAc, with oxidative chain cleavage as accessory chemistry.

name: Sialidase route
description: Hydrolysis of the terminal alpha-linked sialic acid.

name: Alpha-L-fucosidase route
description: Hydrolysis of terminal alpha-L-fucosyl residues.

name: Alpha-N-acetylgalactosaminidase route
description: Hydrolysis of the core alpha-linked N-acetyl-D-galactosamine.

name: Endo- and exo-polygalacturonase route
description: Backbone endohydrolysis then exo-acting release of D-galacturonate, with methyl-ester removal as accessory chemistry.

name: Lower Entner-Doudoroff route
description: Phosphorylation of 2-dehydro-3-deoxy-D-gluconate and aldol cleavage of the product into pyruvate and D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate.

name: Pectate lyase route
description: Endo- then exo-acting beta-elimination of the galacturonan backbone, followed by oligogalacturonide lyase, ketol isomerase and 5-dehydrogenase chemistry into the branchpoint. Direct entry on esterified pectin and de-esterification are accessory.
